name: Lauffen–Frankfurt three-phase transmission
summary: In 1891 three-phase alternating current was sent about 175 km from Lauffen to a Frankfurt exhibition, lighting lamps and driving a motor, showing long-distance power transmission worked.
description: Three-phase generator, transformers and overhead line from Lauffen to Frankfurt exhibition, supplying lamps and a motor-driven waterfall.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: One trial that showed electrical engineers efficient long-distance transmission was possible; three-phase power systems were then built on its pattern.

why: Frankfurt's 1891 electrical exhibition was organised partly to compare competing electrical systems, and engineers used it to prove distant water power could be delivered by alternating current.
